What we consider a sign of bad luck...

And I didn't think you were so jealous.

examples.trans: Well, was it scary? No, there are such airbags there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'уровый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stern, strict').

examples.text: А я не думала, что ты такой суровый отец.
examples.trans: And I didn't think you were such a stern father.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень суровый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very stern choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'father' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Привет, Лёва. Чего хотел?
examples.trans: Hi, Lyova. What did you want?

examples.text: Алло, Макс, почему ты не на работе?
examples.trans: Hello, Max, why aren't you at work?

examples.text: Точно любовник! Ну не отец же.
examples.trans: Definitely her lover! Well, he's not her father.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('jealous').

examples.text: А я не думал, что ты такая ревнивая.
examples.trans: And I didn't think you were so jealous.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень ревнивый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very jealous choice.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я же говорила, что поссоримся.
examples.trans: I told you we would quarrel.

examples.text: У вас написано, что вы открываетесь в одиннадцать.
examples.trans: Your sign says that you open at eleven.

examples.text: А я вам говорю, что это не французский салат.
examples.trans: And I am telling you that this is not a French salad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, я разберусь. Всё будет нормально.
examples.trans: Yes, I will sort it out. Everything will be fine.

examples.text: Выбрала попроще кого-нибудь! Всё, нам хана теперь.
examples.trans: Should have picked someone simpler! That's it, we are done for now.

examples.text: Ребята, мне всё равно, кто ей нахамил.
examples.trans: Guys, I don't care who was rude to her.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, хорошо. Сейчас приеду.
examples.trans: Fine, all right. I will come over now.

examples.text: Значит, не хочешь по-хорошему?
examples.trans: So you don't want to do this the easy way?

examples.text: Ладно, не хочешь хорошего, включу плохого.
examples.trans: Fine, if you don't want the good father, I will turn on the bad one.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: У вас написано, что вы открываетесь в одиннадцать.
examples.trans: Your sign says that you open at eleven.

examples.text: А можно меня не учить? Мне давно не пятнадцать лет.
examples.trans: And can you not lecture me? I haven't been fifteen for a long time.

examples.text: На моей кухне тебе всегда будет пятнадцать.
examples.trans: In my kitchen you will always be fifteen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'except', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он вообще кроме рыбы ничего не может.
examples.trans: He cannot do anything at all except fish.

examples.text: Я звоню мужу! Он вообще закроет ваш ресторан.
examples.trans: I am calling my husband! He will shut your restaurant down completely.

examples.text: Вас можно поздравить! Лёва, не скромничай.
examples.trans: Congratulations are in order! Lyova, don't be modest.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.text: Ну, кроме чёрной кошки, конечно.
examples.trans: Well, except for a black cat, of course.

examples.text: Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри.
examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'cat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Откуда в ресторане кошка?
examples.trans: Where would a cat in a restaurant come from?

examples.text: Ну, кроме чёрной кошки, конечно.
examples.trans: Well, except for a black cat, of course.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, я же тоже нормальный.
examples.trans: Of course, I am normal too.

examples.text: Ну, кроме чёрной кошки, конечно.
examples.trans: Well, except for a black cat, of course.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу.
examples.trans: Of course I'll help.
